title: Discount Calculator - Calculate Sale Price & Savings
description: Calculate final sale prices, total dollars saved, stacked double discounts, and sales tax instantly. Free online discount calculator.
quickAnswer: To find the final sale price and total savings, enter the original item price and discount percentage. You can add a secondary stacked coupon and local sales tax to see exact out-of-pocket costs. Calculations use half-up cent rounding to match retail point-of-sale registers and consumer protection guidelines.

formula.title: Discount & Tax Calculation Formula
formula.expression: Final Price = [(Original Price - (Original Price × Discount1%)) - Stacked Discount] × (1 + Tax%)
formula.explanation: First, apply the primary discount to the original retail price to find the initial savings. Next, apply any secondary stacked coupon to the reduced subtotal (multiplicative, not additive). Finally, compute sales tax on the discounted subtotal using banker-safe half-up cent rounding.

workedExamples.title: Stacked 20% Sale + 10% Store Coupon
steps: Apply secondary 10% coupon to reduced subtotal: $64.00 × 0.10 = $6.40 savings

workedExamples.title: 15% Discount with 8% Sales Tax
steps: Compute 8% sales tax on discounted subtotal: $42.50 × 0.08 = $3.40

commonMistakes.title: Directly Adding Stacked Discounts
commonMistakes.description: A common retail misconception is adding discount rates together (e.g., 20% off + 10% coupon = 30% off). The secondary coupon applies to the already discounted subtotal, yielding 28% total savings.

commonMistakes.title: Applying Sales Tax Before Discounts
commonMistakes.description: In almost all state and provincial tax jurisdictions, sales tax applies strictly to the net price paid after coupons, not the original sticker price.

commonMistakes.title: Cent Rounding Inconsistencies
commonMistakes.description: Retail systems round to the nearest cent at each sequential step. Rounding only at the final total can produce small 1-cent discrepancies with store receipts.

commonMistakes.title: Confusing Percentage Off with Percent of Original Price
commonMistakes.description: A 25% discount means you pay 75% of the original price, not 25% of the original price.

howto.description: Step-by-step instructions for calculating retail discounts, stacked coupons, and sales tax.

steps.name: Select Currency & Original Price

faqs.q: How do you calculate the final discounted price of an item?
faqs.a: Multiply the original sticker price by the discount percentage divided by 100 to find total savings, then subtract the savings from the original price to determine the final sale price.

faqs.q: Why does a 20% sale plus a 10% coupon not equal 30% total discount?
faqs.a: Because stacked store coupons apply to the already reduced sale subtotal rather than the original sticker price. A $100 item reduced by 20% becomes $80; applying 10% off $80 saves $8, bringing the final price to $72 (28% overall savings, not 30%).

faqs.q: Is sales tax calculated before or after applying discounts?
faqs.a: In retail store purchases, sales tax is calculated on the net discounted subtotal after all promotional store discounts and coupons have been applied.

faqs.q: Can I calculate stacked double discounts with this tool?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your primary sale discount percentage in the first field and your secondary store coupon percentage in the optional stacked discount field.

faqs.q: Is any financial data transmitted to a server?
faqs.a: No. All discount calculations execute locally inside your web browser using JavaScript. No price numbers or financial inputs leave your device.

faqs.q: Can this calculator support international currencies like Pounds and Euros?
faqs.a: Yes. Use the currency dropdown selector to switch between Dollars ($), Pounds (£), Euros (€), Yen (¥), and Rupees (₹).

faqs.q: What is an effective discount percentage?
faqs.a: The effective discount percentage is your total dollar savings divided by the original price, expressed as a single equivalent percentage.
